evidence: The existing Multc Lean/Phase IIa subset uses independently implemented published probability rules. The Multc99 2.1 institutional archive was recovered on October 8, 2026, and its unchanged C kernel now supplies boundary, elicitation and planning references for the general Python workflow; see docs/multc99-source.json and research/multc99-audit.md. Multc Lean native duration timing is now recovered and verified through original x86 instructions with explicit boundaries/draws; see docs/multc-legacy-duration-source.json. Native boundary conversion and full workflow remain open. No original binary or C source is bundled.

sources.role: Multc Lean version, scope and fixed historical-rate addition in version 2.1.
Multc99 version and broader multiple-outcome command-line scope.
Thall-Simon-Estey marginal beta rules, N=30 numerical example, full versus reachable boundaries, joint outcome scenarios and look-ahead accrual.

Input ranges, margin conventions, pretrial rejection, cohorts, scenario order, exact operating characteristics and separate duration simulation. Original software redistribution is restricted; no original code or binaries are redistributed.

sources.author: John Venier
sources.role: Multc99 Phase IIa fixed-reference probability rule, complementary response cutoff, N=15 numerical tables and distinct display conventions. Final-cap placeholders are not posterior adverse-outcome thresholds.

Minimum/cohort enrollment rules and suspension only when pending outcomes could change the decision. The calendar replay implements this logic with explicit endpoint delays and a documented accrual-open-clock convention; native generated timing and aggregate duration parity remain outside its scope.
Recovered general Multc99 C implementation, README terms and example transcript; source-kernel reference execution and corrected Python workflows.
Recovered Multc Lean DLL, guide and redistribution terms; bounded x86 duration references with external RNG/vector services substituted.

method_reference: Thall, Simon and Estey (1995), Bayesian sequential monitoring designs for single-arm clinical trials with multiple outcomes, Statistics in Medicine 14:357-379.
validation_reference: tools/reference_multc.R generates independent direct beta integrals, fixed-reference boundaries and full paired-outcome path enumeration. tools/reference_multc_calendar.R adds five explicit-timing replay examples using direct beta tails and enumeration of hypothetical pending completions. Neither script contains native program source.
